mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the prediction is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
regime_hint: tightening phase of the Fed funds rate
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during such rate spikes (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not cross the 4% threshold.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) followed by a subsequent decline are a leading indicator of a labor market softening, which precedes a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases then decreases in the next two months
failure_condition: 60-day returns remain positive despite the labor signal, or the PAYEMS pattern does not reoccur in subsequent windows.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in home sales (HOUST) above 2% of the prior month's level predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals resilient consumer demand.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day return when HOUST exceeds threshold, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 3% in two consecutive months predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return due to supply-side contraction.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not negative when trigger occurs, or INDPRO does not show the required decline pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as expectations of future disinflation boost equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive when CPIAUCSL declines as predicted (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 4% and a drop in manufacturing payrolls (not available in proxies, so using RSAFS as proxy for manufacturing activity decline) predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 return due to weak labor market momentum.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not negative when both triggers occur, or UNRATE does not exceed 4% while RSAFS declines.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in retail employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 2% of the prior month's level in a post-recession context is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to renewed consumer confidence.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 1.02 * previous month's value and macro context is post-recession recovery
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day return when PAYEMS rises by >2% in recovery context.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in consumer demand proxies (combination of GDPC1 decline of 10% and RSAFS < 600M) over one month predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals supply-demand imbalance.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not negative when both proxies trigger the condition.
